First, let's calculate ${x}^{4}\cdot p(x):$

$$
{x}^{4}\cdot p(x)={x}^{4}\cdot (-5{x}^{2})=-5{x}^{6}
$$

When we divide the two functions ${x}^{4}\cdot p(x)$ and $q(x),$ we get a constant, and the limit of a constant is just the constant itself:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{{x}^{4}\cdot p(x)}{q(x)} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-5{x}^{6}}{(9{x}^{6})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }(-\frac{5}{9}) \\  & =-\frac{5}{9}\end{aligned}
$$
